extracted.intended_audience: Prospective authors submitting to MAA Convergence; mathematics instructors (K–16) preparing classroom materials that connect history and mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing submissions to MAA Convergence that use the history of mathematics to teach mathematics in K–16 settings (emphasis on grades 8–14). Describes required framing (classroom application) and enumerates acceptable types of classroom-connected contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal mission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions to MAA Convergence are required to further the journal’s mission of using the history of mathematics to teach mathematics in undergraduate institutions and schools (specifically, for mathematical subjects in the K–16 curriculum, with a particular emphasis on topics studied in grades 8–14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should explicitly connect historical material to mathematics teaching; target audience is instructors and students in K–16, especially grades 8–14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include well-defined classroom application
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission to MAA Convergence must include a well-defined discussion of when, where, and how the historical content of the article can be used in a practical way in the mathematics classroom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should describe concrete implementation details (timing, level, activities, expected outcomes). Even if materials were not field-tested, articulate potential classroom uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission field testing not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Although MAA Convergence authors often share materials that they have employed in their own classrooms, the editors recognize that pre-submission field testing is not always possible. Thus, some submitters may need help articulating potential classroom applications for the historical concepts addressed in their articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors allow submissions that lack classroom trial data; authors should nevertheless clearly explain plausible classroom uses and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guided reading of primary sources
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A Series of Mini-projects from TRIUMPHS: TRansforming Instruction in Undergraduate Mathematics via Primary Historical Sources' and 'The French Connection: Borda, Condorcet and the Mathematics of Voting Theory' — submissions can present structured activities for students to read and work with original historical mathematical texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-contained classroom lessons
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Apportionment: What's Your Fair Share? – An Activity for Liberal Arts and High School Students' and 'Things Certain and Uncertain' — provide ready-to-use lessons or activities aimed at particular student levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises from historical treatises or textbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercises From Historical Treatises or Textbooks
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Helping Ada Lovelace with her Homework: Classroom Exercises from a Victorian Calculus Course' and 'Mabel Sykes: A Life Untold and an Architectural Geometry Book Rediscovered' — adapt historical exercises for modern classrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explorations inspired by historical material
rubrics_metrics.description: Explorations Inspired by or Related to Historical Material
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Mathematical Mysteries of Rapa Nui with Classroom Activities' and 'Need the Area of a Triangle? The Pope Can Help!' — create inquiry projects or explorations motivated by historical topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative approaches for conceptual difficulties
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative Ways of Thinking About a Mathematical Concept when the 'Traditional' 21st-Century Textbook Approach isn't Clicking with Students
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'An Analysis of the First Proofs of the Heine-Borel Theorem' — present historical approaches that offer different conceptual viewpoints useful for teaching when standard methods fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course outlines and experience reports
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'A Mathematical History Tour: Reflections on a Study Abroad Program' and 'Discovering the Beauty of Science' — describe full-course designs or reported experiences of courses that integrate history and mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion prompts and out-of-class essays
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A Writing Intensive General Education History of Mathematics Course' and interdisciplinary course descriptions — provide prompts, essay assignments, or discussion designs informed by historical material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptions of potential student research projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of Potential Student Research Projects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Building a Book: HathiTrust, Ancestry.com, Serendipity, and Lifetime Interests' — outline feasible student research topics and projects rooted in historical sources or methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of replica historical objects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Bridging the Gap Between Theory and Practice: Astronomical Instruments' — provide instructions and pedagogical rationale for building historical mathematical/astronomical instruments or models for classroom use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools for identifying and utilizing primary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools for Identifying and Utilizing Primary Sources in the Classroom
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Online Museum Collections in the Mathematics Classroom' and 'The Educational Times Database: Building an Online Database...' — present resources, databases, or methods teachers can use to find and integrate primary sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processes for incorporating history into teaching practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes for incorporating history into the professional practice of one’s teaching techniques, methodology, or philosophy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Euler and the Bernoullis: Learning by Teaching' and 'Why History of Mathematics?' — discuss strategies and reflective practices for teachers to integrate history into pedagogy and professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informative background articles for instructors
rubrics_metrics.description: Informative background articles that enhance an instructor’s understanding of a specific course; may include general suggestions that can be infused into one’s teaching but that may not have been designed for direct use with students
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Recreational Problems in Medieval Mathematics' — provide historical background or context useful to instructors even if not packaged as a student-facing lesson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to additional classroom resources
rubrics_metrics.description: For additional examples of classroom connections, see MAA Convergence’s Classroom Resources Index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can consult the journal's Classroom Resources Index for further exemplars and models of acceptable classroom-connection submissions.
